filter_tradeoff_insights: FREEHOLD is the binding constraint in D19 Bartley/Woodleigh: that entire modern MRT-linked belt (Bartley Ridge, Botanique, Park Colonial, Woodleigh Residences, Bartley Vue) is 99-yr leasehold. Insisting on freehold there eliminates every large, new, transit-connected project - you are left with boutique FH (The Quinn) or nothing.

The >=1,000 sqft + $2.2M cap (=<=$2,200 psf) now sits BELOW where most freehold 3BR trades in-scope. The band survives only in three pockets: D19 Kovan/Serangoon FH, D14 Eunos/Paya Lebar FH, and inland D15 Joo Chiat/Katong FH. Trophy D15 seafront (Amber/Meyer, $2,300-3,000 psf) is entirely out of reach.

UNIT-COUNT and FREEHOLD pull in opposite directions in this scope. The 'hidden 3BR stack in a large development' thesis mostly fails: large projects here are leasehold (fail tenure) and the large FH ones (Amber belt, Blossoms) are above cap. Large-project + freehold + in-band is close to an empty set - the realistic supply is boutique/older FH.

MOVEMENT signal: Tangerine Grove (tracked FH, D19) asking has jumped from ~$1,404 psf historical to ~$1,862 psf, pricing its 3BR just over the cap. A tracked project pricing itself OUT of band is the week's clearest sign that D19 Paya-Lebar-side freehold is firming - the cap will bite harder over time unless size is flexed up (bigger unit = lower required PSF).

TENURE flex is the single highest-leverage relaxation: dropping to 99-yr opens Bartley/Woodleigh's large modern stock at similar or lower PSF. SIZE flex up (accepting 1,300-1,500 sqft) lowers the required PSF and is what makes Palm Grove and Jade viable. PRICE-floor flex down (~$1.8-2.0M) would capture The Quinn's standard 3BR and Fiorenza's stale-looking listing.
